The northern section of the Danajon Bank, which is located in the Central Visayas islands of the Philippines
is
 a shallow, tropical reef system that supports a multi-species ﬁshery  that is primarily artisanal and
subsistence
 in nature. A persisting management and regulatory challenge in the area is the continued
use
 of illegal ﬁshing  gears that are deemed destructive by either their manner of operation or technical
design.
